**Crédit Agricole takes full ownership of Worldline merchant payments venture**

*The French bank's buyout of Worldline's stake in their joint merchant payments business signals a broader pattern of large European banks reclaiming direct control of payment acceptance.*

Crédit Agricole has acquired Worldline's stake in Cawl, the merchant payment services joint venture the two established in 2023, giving the bank full ownership. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The move comes as Worldline continues to retrench following a difficult period that has seen its market capitalisation collapse and strategic reviews of several business lines. For Crédit Agricole, taking direct control of merchant acquiring aligns with a trend visible across European banking, where large institutions are pulling payment capabilities back in-house rather than outsourcing them. Crédit Agricole has been notably active in payments this year, having also completed France's first production agentic payment in late June.

For Worldline, the disposal reduces its operational footprint further at a time when the company is under pressure to simplify. The transaction raises questions about the viability of the bank-processor joint venture model that was fashionable in European acquiring just a few years ago.

*Sources: [Crédit Agricole buys Worldline out of merchant payments JV](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48040/crdit-agricole-buys-worldline-out-of-merchant-payments-jv) — Finextra*

**PSR says mandatory fraud reimbursement is cutting APP scam losses in the UK**

*The Payment Systems Regulator reports fewer victims and higher reimbursement rates under its mandatory APP fraud rules, though the underlying data tells a more complicated story.*

The PSR has published an assessment of its mandatory APP fraud reimbursement policy, claiming it is delivering fewer victims, more money returned and greater firm engagement in fraud prevention. The regulator framed the results as validation of the regime introduced in October 2024.

The picture is not entirely straightforward. Earlier data from the PSR itself, published in June, showed overall APP fraud losses climbing back above £1.3 billion, with reimbursement rates at 89%. Meanwhile, Monzo reported an 85% surge in fraud reimbursement costs under the mandatory rules. The PSR's positive framing suggests it is keen to defend the policy against industry criticism that the reimbursement obligation creates moral hazard and imposes disproportionate costs on sending firms.

The regulator's intervention comes at a politically sensitive moment. UK fraud losses rose to £1.3 billion in the most recent reporting period, and the payments industry continues to argue that the burden-sharing model needs recalibration. Whether the PSR's own assessment will quiet that debate or sharpen it remains to be seen.

*Sources: [PSR lauds results of APP fraud reimbursement policy](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48042/psr-lauds-results-of-app-fraud-reimbursement-policy) — Finextra*

**Digital euro moves closer as PYMNTS examines what ECON committee vote means**

*The European Parliament's ECON committee approval of the ECB's digital euro negotiating mandate marks a procedural milestone, but the practical and political obstacles between approval and a 2029 launch remain substantial.*

Following the ECON committee's backing of the digital euro negotiating mandate in late June, attention is turning to what the timeline and design choices mean in practice. The ECB is targeting a 2029 launch, and the committee vote moves the proposal toward full parliamentary consideration.

The digital euro sits at the intersection of several live debates in European payments: sovereignty concerns that have driven initiatives such as Wero and UKPI, the role of private-sector stablecoins after Open USD's launch with Visa and Mastercard backing, and open banking providers' concerns that the digital euro's design could lock them out of the ecosystem. The trade body warning in June that the current proposal risks excluding open banking firms has not yet been resolved in the legislative text.

The 2029 target is ambitious given that full parliamentary and Council negotiations have not yet begun, and design questions around offline functionality, privacy, holding limits and intermediary roles remain open. The ECB's Cipollone has positioned the digital euro as a complement to private payments rather than a competitor, but that framing will be tested as the legislation advances.

*Sources: [Europe Wants Its Own Digital Money Moment](https://www.pymnts.com/news/payments-innovation/2026/europe-wants-its-own-digital-money-moment/) — PYMNTS*

**Thought Machine crosses $100 million revenue as core banking modernisation accelerates**

*The cloud-native core banking vendor's milestone reflects sustained demand for platform replacement across banks and payment firms, though the market remains intensely competitive.*

Thought Machine has confirmed it surpassed $100 million in total revenue for the financial year ending December 2025, verified through audited accounts filed this month. The company, which provides cloud-native core banking and payments technology, counts several large banks among its clients.

The milestone is notable less for the figure itself than for what it indicates about the core banking replacement cycle. European banks are under pressure from instant payments mandates, open banking requirements and the proliferation of new payment methods such as Wero and variable recurring payments, all of which strain legacy infrastructure. Thought Machine competes with vendors such as 10x Banking, Mambu and Finzly, as well as incumbent providers modernising their own platforms.

Reaching $100 million in revenue places Thought Machine in a small cohort of next-generation core banking providers that have achieved meaningful commercial scale. Whether the company can sustain growth will depend on converting large-bank proof-of-concept deployments into full migrations, a process that remains slow and complex across the industry.

*Sources: [Thought Machine hits revenue milestone](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110336/thought-machine-hits-revenue-milestone) — Finextra*
